title: Laredo City Council Votes to Continue Downtown Business Improvement District
excerpt: Laredo City Council voted Monday night to continue the downtown business improvement district while seeking feedback from the commercial property owners who pay into it, and asking for more information about the fees and foreclosures.
content:
Laredo City Council voted Monday night to continue the downtown business improvement district, while seeking feedback from the commercial property owners who pay into it, according to KGNS.

Council also wants more information about the district's fees and foreclosures, according to the report. The article did not give a vote tally or dollar amounts.

In another vote, council approved a change to the area covered by a border surveillance agreement on city land. Staff said the agreement is for technology, not a border wall, according to the report.

Council also discussed police grant funding and concerns about surveillance cameras, according to the report.

A survey shown by KGNS found that 69% of people surveyed see downtown negatively, with the top priorities listed as security at 82%, parking at 82%, cleaning at 81%, economic development at 50% and lighting at 48%.

Source: KGNS, Nov. 16, 2026.
